questions.title: Which DRC province will WHO identify as experiencing a surge in weekly Ebola cases in mid-September 2026?
questions.background: The Democratic Republic of Congo declared an Ebola outbreak in May 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : WHO public statements about the DRC Ebola outbreak, including statements quoted in contemporaneous reputable news reporting. Resolution Window : Resolve to the province explicitly identified by WHO as experiencing surging weekly Ebola cases in its outbreak assessment publicly reported between September 10 and September 16, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: Updated on three substantive 2026-09-04 epidemiological developments (GB News/Airfinity Sept 4, Outbreak News Today/DRC MOH Sept 4, Reuters/Straits Times Sept 4). First, Airfinity's Sept 4 subnational modelling noted national 7-day averages dipped 16% in late August but warned this masks sharp provincial divergence: 'While case growth has begun to slow in Ituri, it has merely levelled off in North Kivu province and is picking up pace in Haut-Uele.' Second, DRC MOH's latest daily breakdown (6,342 total cases, 3,072 deaths across 60/151 HZs as of Sept 2) reported 92 new confirmed cases: Ituri 60 (65.2% of daily vs 81.4% cumulative), North Kivu 25 (27.2%, double its ~14% cumulative share), Haut-Uele 5 (5.4% plus 1 ETC death—up markedly from late-Aug DON616 when all four smaller provinces combined had just 7/81 daily cases), Tshopo 2 (now 7/23 affected HZs, more HZs than Haut-Uele's 6/13 or Bas-Uele's 3/11), and 0 each in Bas-Uele and South Kivu. Third, AFC/M23 rebels confirmed on Sept 3-4 a brand-new Ebola case in Kayna health zone (North Kivu, near Lubero) in a 21-year-old arriving from Butembo, breaching >2 months of zero cases in rebel-held territory as schools reopen.
